solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Glaswegian drinking heavily with gold chain can start to gibber

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
ch is the abbreviation for chain, the old surveying measure
a can is a tin

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of gibber

explanation.surface: A drunk Glaswegian in gold jewellery is on the verge of talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chain' and 'can' look like a necklace and a verb, but each is a standalone abbreviation or synonym. WAUCHT is Scots for a big swig, so WAUCHTING is drinking deeply.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots verb waucht means to quaff in large draughts, so the participle describes a Scotsman swilling his drink.

clue.text: Change wickets and declare

parts.note: W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wickets
to aver is to declare or assert

explanation.surface: A cricket captain switches the batting order and declares the innings closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change wickets' and 'declare' sound like cricket tactics; in cricket a captain declares to end his side's innings early.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver is to fluctuate or shift back and forth, an unsteady kind of altering one's position.

clue.text: Poet's blank mind sure hasn't succeeded in composition

indicators.note: composing means putting together afresh, so the remaining letters are rearranged
what something hasn't got is missing from it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
s is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A poet with writer's block finds his confident mind has failed him mid-composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' flags a literary spelling: UNRIMED is the old form of unrhymed, and blank verse is verse that does not rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Blank verse lacks rhyme, so a poet would call such lines unrhymed, spelt in the archaic way.

clue.text: Never finished, sharpen opening form of address

indicators.note: something never finished lacks its ending, so each word loses its last letter

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen a blade
an orifice is an opening

explanation.surface: Someone keeps polishing the opening line of a speech without ever completing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Never finished' covers both words: each of the two synonyms loses its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorific is a title of respect such as Sir or Dr used when addressing someone.

clue.text: Being this callous would make "wily" descriptive of the missus?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: the clue asks for a word meaning hard and unfeeling

definitions.text: would make "wily" descriptive of the missus?
definitions.meaning: setter's reading: put the chemical symbol for iron into the heart of wily and you get wifely, an adjective for a wife

explanation.surface: A man wonders whether calling his wife cunning makes him heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, the answer means 'with iron in its heart': FE inside WI-LY makes WIFELY, which describes the missus.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a heart of metal is pitiless and unfeeling, which is exactly what callous means.

clue.text: Gossip, the extremes of which absorb you in DMs

indicators.note: to absorb is to take something inside, so one piece goes within the other
extremes are the two ends, so just the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the clue's opening word
in text messages you is written as the single letter U

explanation.surface: Gossip that spreads to you through direct messages on social media.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word does double duty: it is the definition and also supplies its own outer letters. DMs are direct messages, where text-speak rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Gup is an Anglo-Indian slang word for idle chatter or scandal, a dialect synonym for rumour-mongering.

clue.text: Norwegian group among Kuala Lumpur's Jewish community

indicators.note: to be among things is to sit in their midst, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the initial letters of the two words of the Malaysian capital's name
a-ha were the Norwegian pop band behind Take On Me

explanation.surface: A band from Norway turns up in the Jewish quarter of Kuala Lumpur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norwegian group' suggests a folk society or political body, but it is the 1980s pop trio.
explanation.definitionFit: Kahal is the Hebrew term for a congregation or self-governing community of Jews.

clue.text: Lifted up by machine primarily, fine seaweed

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting means reading from bottom to top
primarily means first of all, so each word gives only its initial letter

parts.note: the initial letters of these three words
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: Good-quality seaweed is hauled out of the sea by a mechanical harvester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted up' reads as one phrase, but only 'Lifted' signals the reversal; 'up' is fodder for its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kombu is the edible kelp used in Japanese cooking, notably to make dashi stock.

clue.text: Aircraft designer drawing stuff into back section

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside

parts.note: the heel is the back part of a foot or shoe
ink is the stuff used for drawing

explanation.surface: An aircraft designer sketching plans for the tail section of a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back section' sounds like part of an aeroplane but means the rear of a foot. Ernst Heinkel built German aircraft including wartime bombers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernst Heinkel founded the German manufacturer that produced the He 111 bomber and the first jet aircraft.

clue.text: Large app for images preserves vintage wallpaper

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: Insta is the casual name for Instagram, the photo-sharing app
a cru is a vineyard or wine of a given growth, that is a vintage

explanation.surface: A big photo app keeps old-fashioned wallpaper designs in its archive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vintage' looks like an adjective for the wallpaper, but it is a noun for a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincrusta is a Victorian embossed wall covering made from linseed paste, still sold as a heavy relief wallpaper.

clue.text: After six, odd stranger in DC covered area around building once

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
rando is American slang for a random, odd stranger; DC places it in the US

explanation.surface: After six o'clock a weird stranger in Washington lurks on the porch of an old building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just orders the pieces: the numeral comes first. 'Once' marks the answer as an obsolete spelling of veranda.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed gallery along the outside of a house, and virando is a historic variant of that word.

clue.text: Do weights but not run, old fruit

indicators.note: but not means excluding something, so one letter is taken out

parts.note: to pump iron is to lift weights
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Advice to lift weights but skip running, addressed to an old chum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old fruit' is a dated British form of address for a friend, but here it is a fruit that is old. Pumpion is the archaic word for pumpkin.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpion was the Elizabethan name for a pumpkin, so it is a fruit name from long ago.

clue.text: Someone rambling without a map-reading tool

indicators.note: without means lacking, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: a roamer is someone who rambles or wanders
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hiker setting off without a map-reading tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'without a map-reading tool' one phrase, but 'without a' is the instruction and the tool is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A romer is a small transparent scale used with a compass to read off grid references on a map.

clue.text: Pick-up line not needed for success in northeastern estuary

indicators.note: placing one thing in another puts it inside

parts.note: the Humber is the estuary on England's northeast coast

indicators.note: something not needed is left out, so one letter goes

parts.note: luck is good fortune or success
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone claims you can pull in an estuary town without a chat-up line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick-up line' looks like a chat-up line, but the hyphenated 'Pick-up' alone is the definition, a guitar component.
explanation.definitionFit: A humbucker is a twin-coil electric-guitar pickup designed to cancel out the hum single coils produce.

clue.text: Fundamental operating system code in core Kremlin hacked

indicators.note: hacked code has been broken into and mangled, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Essential operating system software at the heart of the Kremlin has been breached.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a cyberattack news story; 'core' feels like part of the definition but belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A microkernel is a minimal kernel providing only the basic services of an operating system, the bare foundation.

clue.text: Looking back, when one emerged as a person

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: DOB, date of birth, records when a person emerged into the world

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on the moment they first came into their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When one emerged' sounds like a coming-of-age moment, but it means birth, abbreviated as on forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Bod is informal British slang for a person or individual, short for body.

clue.text: Sweet American variety in Idahoan city

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: Boise is the state capital of Idaho
A is the abbreviation for American
var is the botanical abbreviation for variety

explanation.surface: A dessert of American origin served in a city in Idaho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet American variety' reads as one phrase, as if the dessert were American; only 'Sweet' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Bavaroise is the French name for Bavarian cream, a set custard dessert, so it is a pudding.

clue.text: Betrothal of French daughters, keeping eg Fleming around

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: filles is French for daughters
Ian Fleming wrote the James Bond novels
ca, for circa, means around

explanation.surface: A French family's daughters get engaged while a Fleming hangs around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like the container signal, but it supplies the abbreviation for circa; 'keeping' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiançailles is the French word for an engagement to marry, used in English for a formal betrothal.

clue.text: Superfan invading sepulchre right away

indicators.note: an invader forces its way inside, so one piece enters another

parts.note: to sepulchre, as a verb, is to bury or inter
a stan is slang for an obsessive fan, from the Eminem song

explanation.surface: An obsessive fan breaks into a tomb straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sepulchre' is normally a noun, a tomb, but here it is the verb meaning to entomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Instanter is a legal Latin adverb meaning immediately or at once.

clue.text: Cases of blistering cavities son developed

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy's tooth cavities flared into painful blisters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavities' looks medical enough to be part of the definition, but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesication is the medical term for blister formation, so its plural means instances of it.

clue.text: Drink noisily, using uncapped soda for liberal American cough medicine cocktail

indicators.note: using, with for, means the soda letters are put to use in place of the liberal's letter
for means standing in place of, so the soda letters take the place of the liberal's letter

parts.note: to slurp is to drink noisily

indicators.note: uncapped means the top, the first letter, is taken off

parts.note: fizz is a fizzy drink such as soda

explanation.surface: Instructions for mixing a cough-syrup cocktail by noisily drinking soda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncapped' takes the F off FIZZ, and those letters go in 'for' the L in SLURP. Sizzurp is US slang for a drink of codeine cough syrup mixed with soda.
explanation.definitionFit: Sizzurp, also called purple drank, is an American recreational mix of prescription cough syrup with soft drink and candy.

clue.text: Accessory with feathers from duck displacing undergarment's contents

indicators.note: to displace is to push something out and take its place

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
a bra is an undergarment
the contents of a three-letter word are its middle letter

explanation.surface: A feathery fashion item made from a duck that has replaced the lining of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' and 'feathers' together make a bird picture, but the duck is cricket's zero score.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a long fluffy scarf of feathers worn round the neck.

clue.text: Australian with a small pouch is to stake 100, 1000 dollars

parts.note: to bet is to stake money
a ton is slang for a hundred
G, a grand, is a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: An Australian with a small purse puts a hundred, or a thousand dollars, on a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small pouch' suggests a wallet, but the Australian is an animal and the pouch is marsupial.
explanation.definitionFit: A bettong is a small rat-kangaroo native to Australia, a marsupial that carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Storm about variable mineral aggregate ultimately mined in precarious situation?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer word goes round the rest

parts.note: to rage is to storm
z is a standard algebraic variable
ore is rock containing an aggregate of minerals

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of mined

explanation.surface: A storm hits a mining operation, leaving everyone in a perilous spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is figurative: a razor's edge is a fine line, not literal steel.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on a razor edge is an idiom for being in a critically delicate or dangerous position.

clue.text: Scottish bar was supposedly the Archbishop of Canterbury

parts.note: the head of an organisation supposedly runs it, past tense here
the Archbishop leads the Church of England, CE, so this is what he ran

explanation.surface: A pub in Scotland was reputedly once the Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a sentence about the Archbishop: he ran the Church of England, the 'supposedly' allowing that he only nominally does.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, a rance is a prop or wooden bar used to brace or shore something up.

clue.text: Would-be cultured return of Lysistrata with lead and every other couple withdrawing

indicators.note: return means the letters come back in reverse order
withdrawing means every other pair of letters is taken out, here the second and fourth pairs
every other couple means alternate pairs of letters, the second and fourth, are the ones affected
with lead, paired with withdrawing, means the leading letter of the play's name goes

explanation.surface: A pretentious revival of Aristophanes' comedy Lysistrata, with its star and half the cast pulling out.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping L leaves YSISTRATA; in pairs that is YS IS TR AT A, and taking out every other pair (IS, AT) leaves YSTRA, which reads backwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Artsy describes someone affecting an interest in the arts, a pretentious would-be aesthete.

clue.text: Indigenous Siberian's shaggy ox just shorn of odd parts

parts.note: the yak is a long-haired ox of Central Asia

indicators.note: cutting away the odd-numbered positions keeps only the even letters

parts.note: second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A Siberian's long-haired ox has just been sheared of its odd bits.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Siberian reads as 'Siberian is', the link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yakuts, or Sakha, are a Turkic people native to northeastern Siberia.

clue.text: Uproar in Québec, at the US's private backing for reptile

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the whole string reads the other way

parts.note: a din is an uproar
au is French for 'at the', the language of Québec
a GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A commotion in Québec as an American soldier backs away from a reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Québec' looks like a location in the story, but it tells you to translate 'at the' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: An iguanid is any lizard of the iguana family, so it is one kind of reptile.

clue.text: Mean and disgruntled, by the look of it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: excellent, as in hip-hop slang where a mean guitarist is a great one

definitions.text: disgruntled, by the look of it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word looks like a cut-down 'deaf' or 'defiant', a scowling sort of word, which the setter treats playfully

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' tempts as nasty or average; in slang it is high praise, matching the hip-hop adjective. The second half is a loose, visual joke rather than a strict meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Def is street slang for excellent or cool, the same approving sense that mean carries in phrases like a mean cook.

clue.text: Bailiff demolished hut in sheltered place

indicators.note: this preposition places one thing within another, so one string goes inside the other

parts.note: a nook is a sheltered corner

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked apart, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bailiff knocks down a shack in a sheltered spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuthook is a Shakespearean insult for a constable or bailiff, one who hooks people as a hooked pole pulls down nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare uses nuthook as contemptuous slang for a beadle or officer who arrests people, much like a bailiff.

clue.text: Quiet comeback of this album will supply docile followers

indicators.note: comeback means the word is turned back to front
will supply describes the clue as a sum: quiet plus the reversed answer supplies the followers, so taking quiet away leaves the rest

parts.note: sheeple is slang for people who follow the crowd like sheep
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A quiet comeback album that pleases a meek and loyal fan base.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads SH plus the answer reversed equals SHEEPLE; so remove SH and reverse EEPLE. An elpee is an LP spelt out, the classic crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Elpee is the spelt-out form of LP, a long-playing record or album, so 'this album' is one.

clue.text: Common law to divide land after switching sides

indicators.note: after, read with switching sides, means each word is taken as it stands once its left and right letters have traded places

parts.note: to fork is to divide or split into branches

indicators.note: sides are left and right, so an L and an R trade places in each word

parts.note: to light is to land or settle, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A dispute over dividing territory after a change of allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: In FORK the R (right) becomes L (left), and in LIGHT the L becomes R. 'land' is the verb, as in alighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Folkright is an old English term for the customary law of the people, as opposed to written statute.
